nodes.label: Actions on a Change
nodes.rationale: Apply is not phase-locked: it can run whenever tasks exist, after partial implementation, or interleaved with other actions. If implementation reveals design issues, update artifacts rather than treating phases as a lockstep pipeline.

nodes.label: Explore Stance
nodes.rationale: Explore mode is a thinking stance, not a workflow and not implementation. Answering design questions is never consent to write; confirmation covers only the named scope. Implementation is handed to /opsx-propose, never started from explore.

nodes.label: Planning Boundary
nodes.rationale: Selecting this workflow authorizes planning artifacts only, even if the user asked to build or fix something. Do not edit project code or start apply in the same response; wait for a new request.

nodes.label: Intelligent Merging
nodes.rationale: Agent-driven merge is used instead of overwrite so a scenario can be added without copying an entire requirement. Preserve unmentioned main-spec content in existing order; a MODIFIED block must carry every surviving scenario or validate/archive will reject it.

nodes.label: Coherence Review
nodes.rationale: A generic update request is a coherence review across existing artifacts, not creation of missing ones. Edits may flow in any direction; build order is only a reading order. Confirm every write; never edit implementation code.

nodes.label: Update vs Start Fresh
nodes.rationale: If the request changes the change's intent rather than refining it, ask for a distinct unused change name and recommend openspec new change instead of rewriting the existing plan.

nodes.label: Jev
nodes.rationale: Jev is TypeSafe AI's System One decision model, not a chat model and not a text generator. Current phase is research and repo tooling only.

nodes.label: TypeSafe
nodes.rationale: TypeSafe is the company and API, not a generic TypeScript MCP library.

nodes.label: Recommended TypeScript MCP Wrapper
nodes.rationale: Later implementation should be a thin TypeScript wrapper around @typesafe-ai/sdk plus the official MCP SDK. Keys live only in TYPESAFE_API_KEY, never in the repo or tool parameters.

nodes.label: Shared MCP Servers Placeholder
nodes.rationale: Register the local TypeSafe/Jev MCP after it is implemented. Secrets must use ${VAR} interpolation and never commit real keys.

nodes.label: Jev
nodes.rationale: Jev evaluates a state plus typed questions and returns structured answers, probabilities, and confidence. It does not generate text, code, or explanations.

nodes.label: TypeSafe
nodes.rationale: TypeSafe is the company and API at https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone plus official JS/Python SDKs, not a generic TypeScript MCP library.

nodes.label: Jev + TypeSafe MCP Research
nodes.rationale: Scope is how to build, not implementing MCP server product logic. Current phase is research only.

nodes.label: Jev
nodes.rationale: Jev is TypeSafe AI's hosted System One decision model, not a chat LLM and not a local runtime. It cannot write mail, code, explanations, or images; it is a calibrated structured judge for routing, review, scoring, and guardrails.

nodes.label: TypeSafe AI
nodes.rationale: TypeSafe means TypeSafe AI the company and its API/SDK, not generic TypeScript type-safe MCP. The repo name primarily means MCP for TypeSafe/Jev, with type-safe implementation as a constraint.

nodes.label: jev-1.13.0
nodes.rationale: Current version. Aliases jev-latest and jev-preview point here today; production thresholds should pin the version because jev-latest drifts.

nodes.label: Scheme A TypeScript MCP Thin Wrapper
nodes.rationale: Recommended because it aligns with the official JS SDK and official MCP TypeScript SDK so types can flow from question definitions to answers; matches the private repo and self-built control; existing jev-mcp repos can be references rather than dependencies; a small first-phase surface can quickly validate agent routing and review. Do not start with a gate/screen/match suite or disguise Jev as a chat model.
nodes.norm_label: scheme a typescript mcp thin wrapper

nodes.label: Scheme B Python MCP
nodes.rationale: Same thin-wrapper idea with FastMCP or the official Python MCP SDK. Fits an existing Python agent stack, but is a weaker match for Cursor and for the typesafe-mcp TypeScript reading of the repo name.

nodes.label: Scheme C Fork Existing jev-mcp
nodes.rationale: Fastest path to a running server. Risks are license, maintenance, official SDK drift, and key handling. Better for product validation than as this repo's product base.

nodes.label: Scheme D Library Only
nodes.rationale: Call @typesafe-ai/sdk from the application directly. MCP is valuable when agents call Jev in a loop; if the caller is always your own backend, MCP is unnecessary.

nodes.label: Scheme E Remote Hosted MCP
nodes.rationale: Streamable HTTP plus local auth fits multi-client sharing of one key. Costs are deploy, auth, and rate limits. Local stdio is simpler and avoids placing the TypeSafe key in the cloud.

nodes.label: TYPESAFE_API_KEY
nodes.rationale: Read only from the environment. Passing a key as a tool parameter or into a transcript is a security incident.

nodes.label: Code-Side Gating
nodes.rationale: Jev confidence describes distribution concentration, not permission to auto-execute. Compute act | review | abstain in code from act_above / review_above thresholds rather than asking Jev whether it may proceed.

nodes.label: Type Safety Guarantees Interface Not Facts
nodes.rationale: Official emphasis: the output space is defined by the request and the model does not invent types. Type safety guarantees the interface, not factual correctness.
nodes.norm_label: type safety guarantees interface not facts

nodes.label: Third-Party jev-mcp Ecosystem
nodes.rationale: Several 2026-09 third-party jev-mcp servers already exist. They validate the direction but differ in quality, maintainers, and licenses, so this repo should differentiate on official SDK use, strict types, structured content, key isolation, and testable gating.

nodes.label: Chinese Artifact Language Rule
nodes.rationale: All artifacts must be written in zh while OpenSpec structural headings and SHALL/MUST keywords stay in English.

nodes.label: Implementation Hold
nodes.rationale: Do not implement MCP server product code until the user asks. Research lives in docs/research-jev-typesafe-mcp.md. When implementation starts, use TypeScript, @typesafe-ai/sdk, official MCP TypeScript SDK, and Zod, with TYPESAFE_API_KEY via environment only.
